translationRepairs: Jing's troops were Qiang and Hu of mixed stock; they jostled those on either side with great insolence. The guards did not flinch or yield—only Buhai and palace attendant Xu Chi stood unmoved at the emperor's side.

Jing's troops were Qiang and Hu of mixed stock; they jostled those on either side with great insolence. The guards were startled and gave way—only Buhai and palace attendant Xu Chi stood unmoved at the emperor's side.
Chapter s0022 lacks 莫 (侍衛者不驚恐辟易), but 唯不害…侍側不動 requires that the other guards did yield; critical editions restore 莫不驚恐辟易, and the proposed idiomatic correctly renders that sense.

Jing's soldiers were all mixed breeds of Qiang and Hu; they charged left and right, very insolent. The guards did not startle or give way—only Buhai and palace attendant Xu Chi stood at the side unmoved.

Jing's soldiers were all mixed breeds of Qiang and Hu; they charged left and right, very insolent. The guards were startled and gave way—only Buhai and palace attendant Xu Chi stood at the side unmoved.
Same unit: the chapter’s 不 without 莫 is corrupt against 唯…不動; editions reading 莫不驚恐辟易 support “were startled and gave way” in the literal.
At the time, emperor Jianwen was confined by Jing, he sent someone to request that Buhai dwell with him; Jing assented, and Buhai waited on him with ever greater care.
When Emperor Jianwen was confined by Jing, he sent someone to request that Buhai dwell with him; Jing assented, and Buhai waited on him with ever greater care.
及簡文為景所幽 is a temporal “when” clause, not discourse “At the time,”; the original also leaves a comma splice, and the proposed wording matches the Chinese and the already-correct literal.
At the time, emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne, he made Buhai a Secretariat gentleman and concurrently director of the Court Tribunal, and thus led his household west.
When Emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne, he made Buhai a Secretariat gentleman and concurrently director of the Court Tribunal, and thus led his household west.

梁元帝立 is a circumstantial “when he took the throne” clause; “At the time,” is unsupported padding and creates a comma splice, while the proposed “When Emperor Yuan…” matches the Chinese and the literal.
Houzhu thereupon ordered attendant Wenqing Shi [2], "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; grant him one hundred piculs of grain."
Houzhu thereupon ordered attendant Shi Wenqing [2], "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; grant him one hundred piculs of grain."
施文慶 is surname 施 (Shi) plus given name 文慶 (Wenqing); “Wenqing Shi” reverses Chinese name order, and the proposed Shi Wenqing restores it.
Houzhu thereupon ordered the attendant Wenqing Shi, [to say]: "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; one hundred piculs of grain may be granted."
Houzhu thereupon ordered the attendant Shi Wenqing, [to say]: "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; one hundred piculs of grain may be granted."
Same name order error in the literal: 施文慶 must be Shi Wenqing, not Wenqing Shi.
When mourning ended, as a kinsman by marriage and a younger clansman he was admitted to audience; Emperor Wu of Liang saw Hao emaciated, sighed a long while, and said to father and son Zichan:
When mourning ended, as a kinsman by marriage and a younger clansman he was admitted to audience; Emperor Wu of Liang saw Hao emaciated, sighed a long while, and said to his father Zichan:
其父子產 means “his father Zichan” (父 + name 子產), as already in s0122; “father and son Zichan” invents a father–son pair.
